title: Column Adder
description: Line up the points, add place by place with carries across the point, give whole numbers their point, and see that order and adding zero change nothing.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit. With navDots the dots are controls in AI mode too: a tap on a dot starts that phase.

stage.sizing: the frame is min(100vw, 177.78vh) wide and min(100vh, 56.25vw) tall (dvh where supported); the svg fills it. Nothing scrolls.

bands.header: 0 to 80. One line: the tool name, a measured dot, the phase concept; Hint, sound and restart as round controls far right.
bands.canvas: 92 to 640. One rounded card holding the key at its top right (Answer, Close, Enter, Next, or the Yes / No keys; no question bar), the working area (the whole card until Answer is tapped) and the answer drawer that slides in from the right; the summary page covers it at the end.
bands.footer: 652 to 900. The mascot at the far left on its ground line, the speech bubble beside it (y 656 to 892, the question and every line, printed), one small dot per phase at the right.

zones.layout: board, key only: no question bar, only its key at the right end of the top row (the question is on the bubble); the working area is the whole card (64, 108, 1472 x 520) until the child taps Answer, when the answer drawer (as tall as the working area, the key on its top row reading Close) slides in from the right
zones.controls: circles r 28 at cx 1388, 1460, 1532, cy 40: Hint (data-control again), sound, restart; 72-unit finger boxes
zones.dots: one small dot per phase at the footer's right (72-unit finger boxes, centred on the bubble), no text; in user AND AI mode each is a button (data-control phase-dot, data-phase k) that starts its phase

stage.noSidebar: There is no sidebar. The canvas takes every unit the chrome can spare.
stage.noScoreBox: There is no score box on the stage. The score leaves on finished and onComplete and is shown once, as stars on the summary page.

writeup.why: Add decimals, whole numbers among them, with the points in one line and carrying across the point, and use the order and zero properties to check a sum.
writeup.look: A column frame with one fixed point line down its middle, decimal cards lined up on it, and an answer row under a ruled line.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Column Adder' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at x sixty-four, y 108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: how many columns have been added, from the right. It is never a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at x sixty-four, y 202. The frame spans x 110 to x 900 from y 230 to y 560, five columns 140 across headed Tens, Ones, Tenths, Hundredths and Thousandths, with the near-black point line at x 400 between Ones and Tenths. Cards sit one per row at y 270, y 350 and y 430, deep blue and labelled Given, sliding until their points sit on the line. A ruled line at y 500 has the answer row under it, where the sum is written green, labelled Sum. A column being added lights amber; a carry is a vermilion 1 labelled Carry that rolls up to the top of the next column to the left, crossing the point line when it comes from the tenths. The tray runs along y 640. The Like, Add, Point first and Swap buttons and the Add zero card stand down the right of the working area at x 960. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at x 1186, y 250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at x 1170, y 368 (388 by 363). The pad is twelve number keys three across with a point key, for setting a decimal with up to three places or typing a sum into the answer slot. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own, and the tools of this chapter share them. A decimal or fraction the question gives is deep blue, with the shaded parts that show it. The result the working reaches, a decimal, a fraction, a sum, a difference or what is left, is green, with its shaded parts. Ten of one place traded for one of the next, a carry in adding or a trade in taking away, is vermilion. A zero written after the point to line decimals up is violet, and so is the point written after a whole number before those zeros. The part taken away, used or poured out is rose. The digit, place or step being worked on now, and the first place where two decimals differ, are amber. A zero holding a place open inside a number is grey, and nothing else on the stage is ever grey. An unshaded part stays warm white inside its near-black outline, the decimal point is near-black ink, and anything dimmed fades to half strength rather than turning grey. Chrome never borrows one of them, and each of those readings survives with the colour taken away, because a part is told by its written label, Given, Answer, Carry, Trade, Added zero, Taken away, Left or Place holder, before it is told by its colour.
writeup.finish: The card shows the last sum in the frame, every point on the one line and every carry still in vermilion above its column.

writeup.delight: On the second phase, when the tenths make ten or more, the vermilion carry hops over the point line like a frog over a stream and lands on top of the ones column with a soft plop.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with the column frame drawn and its point line down the middle. On the first three phases the cards wait in the tray under the frame, and on the third one of them is a whole number with no point. On the fourth two cards are already lined up with their sum in the answer row. One thing moves, once: the first card in the tray, or the Swap button, gives one slow pulse while the voice speaks its opening line, and a finger on it is the whole way in.
writeup.freePlay: Any decimals and whole numbers in the frame, lined up, made like or not, added and swapped. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on lining up the points, carrying, whole numbers with decimals, and order and zero.

onWrong.marks: Nothing is marked, nothing resets, no colour means good or bad. The child's answer stays; the pad re-opens after the traceback.
tracebacks: Phase 1: The cards line up by their points, zeros make like decimals, each column is added from the right and the point drops straight below, ending on the whole sum.
Phase 2: Each column lights from the right and shows its total; the ten rolls on as a carry, across the point too, and the whole sum is written below.
Phase 3: The whole number takes its point after the ones digit, every card lines up by its point, zeros make like decimals, and the columns add to the whole sum.
Phase 4: A prediction: the hand swaps the cards and the pencil adds them again, writing the same sum. Adding 0: the 0 card lines up by its point and the columns add to the whole sum.

voice.opening: A column frame, with one line for every point.
voice.onFreePlay: Free play. Line up any of the cards and add them.
voice.onMiss: the item's own miss line, then the phase's two ladder rungs, shown at once UNDER the pinned instruction and kept until the child acts again
voice.onFinish: Every point in one line, and every carry across.
voice.rules: Silent: nothing is spoken (no device speech, no recorded clips, no Tap to start cover). The speech bubble is the guide: every instruction and hint is one printed page, numbers as words. The lesson is action-driven in every mode: a guide step's instruction stays until the child does the act it names; a wrong act shows that step's hint under the pinned instruction, a wrong answer the next rung of its ladder, and the hint stays unchanged until the child acts again; a right answer's next question, a phase's next phase and the summary's rows follow by themselves after a short celebration. The header's Hint key shows the step's hint or the next rung on demand. What is heard is sound effects (Web Audio), switched by the sound button, on in every mode. In classroom mode nothing waits for a tap except the pieces of a long line (the blinking arrow; a tap, Enter, Space, ArrowRight or PageDown on the bubble shows the next piece), and a tap on the bubble when nothing waits is the teacher's skip.

guide.playsOn: guide steps on phase 1, 2, 3, 4: the phase opens on its first instruction and waits for the child's act (getState guideStep, guideSteps, guideOn); the agent's check() performs the current step; the last act opens the first question. Other phases open on their printed teach lines, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

question.en: Line up the points, then add 5.23 and 1.6.
Now add 4.12 and 3.5 the same way.
Add 2.87 and 3.46, carrying where a column makes ten or more.

items.planAnswer: 3.92. Hundredths: 8 + 4 = 12, so write 2 and carry 1 tenth

question.en: Now add the whole number 6 and 2.35.

items.planAnswer: 8.35. Write 6 as 6.00 first, with its point after the 6

items.planQuestion: Three ribbons are 4 m, 1.85 m and 0.6 m long. What is their total length?

items.planQuestion: Does 2.06 + 5.3 give the same sum as 5.3 + 2.06?

question.en: Will 5.3 + 2.06 give the same sum as 2.06 + 5.3?

items.planQuestion: Is 4.7 + 2.18 the same as 2.18 + 4.7? What is the sum?

question.en: If the cards swap to 2.18 + 4.7, is the sum still the same?

items.planAnswer: Yes. Changing the order does not change the sum, which is 6.88

scoring.wrong: costs nothing, never marked, counted only for first try accuracy
scoring.stars: one for finishing, two at sixty per cent right first time, three at ninety; hidden with the first-try line by showScore false
scoring.phaseMount: a mount scores every phase it plays, from its phase to the last (+5 a question; phases of 3, 3, 3, 3 questions)
scoring.finishCard: stars and the Right first time line under the phase rows on the summary page

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 4 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once. Present: rounded and clamped to one to 4; the tool starts at that phase and, as the NCERT tools do, walks on by itself after each phase's last question (its closing line, then 1.4 s), in user and AI mode alike, through phase 4 to the summary page (a tool with nextKey, runtime r48+: in user mode it waits for the child's blinking Next key instead, after every question and every phase, and the last phase's key opens the summary; AI mode, and a host that mounts one phase without navigableDots, walk on by themselves); finished once, from the summary page.
hostContract.navigableDots: true (or no phase): user mode, the phase dots are controls; otherwise AI mode, the dots show progress and the agent drives window.toolApi.

onProgress.done: questions right so far in this phase

hostContract.emits: every event is dispatched on window and, when framed, posted to window.parent as { type: 'event', name, detail }

getState: toolId, mediaId, mode, mountPhase, phase, phases, conceptId, objectiveIds, step, steps, item, items, stage (teach, demo, ask, win, idle, summary, free), question, questionText, choices, typed, keypadOpen, tries, answered, firstTry, score, maxScore, answerShown (only after the answer), complete, questionCount, muted (the sound effects), speaking (always false: the lesson is silent), voice ("silent"), mascot, summaryRow, played, classroom, held (a classroom's parked piece of a long line), instruction (the pinned line), hint (the hint under it, or null), guideStep / guideSteps / guideOn (a guide-steps phase only), cards, r, aligned, r, columns, carries, sum, swapped, complete

terminalEvent.name: finished
terminalEvent.fires: once per mount, from the summary page after the last phase, 5 s after the page opens (its lines may still be going on); one-shot guarded and re-armed by restart or Play again; never sent at the end of an earlier phase (the tool walks on), and never if Free play or Play again is tapped first

sounds: Web Audio, no files, on in every mode (the sound button switches them): correct, wrong (soft), win at a phase end, cheer at the last, a tick when a piece snaps, and cut, settle and trade where the picture moves
